1. (Currently amended) A battery assembly comprising: an enclosure; a first battery cell positioned within the enclosure; and a first sensor positioned within the enclosure for detecting at least one force influencing the first battery cell, wherein the first sensor is configured to detect mechanical stress or deformation of the first battery cell caused by swelling, expansion, or external pressure.

2. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising an adhesive layer positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, and wherein the adhesive layer is configured to maintain the first sensor in contact with the first battery cell during normal operation.

3. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein at least a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned adjacent at least a portion the first sensor in a plane between the first battery cell and the enclosure.

4. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 3, wherein the adhesive layer extends around at least a portion of the first sensor in the plane.

5. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein a portion of the first sensor extends through a gap in the adhesive layer towards an edge of the first battery cell.

6. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned between the first sensor and one of the first battery cell and the enclosure.

7. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising a deformable element positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, and wherein the deformable element is configured to transmit mechanical forces from the first battery cell to the first sensor.

8. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein: the enclosure comprises an enclosure portion of protective film; and the first sensor is positioned between first battery cell and the enclosure portion, wherein the protective film is configured to isolate the first sensor from external environmental factors while allowing force transmission.

9. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 8, wherein the protective film is a polyester film.

10. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein: the enclosure comprises a plastic case portion; and the first sensor is positioned between first battery cell and the plastic case portion, wherein the plastic case portion is configured to provide structural support while allowing the first sensor to detect forces influencing the first battery cell.

11. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising a second battery cell stacked on top of the first battery cell, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the second battery cell, and wherein the first sensor is configured to detect forces resulting from stacking pressure or relative movement between the first and second battery cells.

12. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 11 further comprising an adhesive layer between the first battery cell and the second battery cell.

13. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein at least a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned adjacent at least a portion the first sensor in a plane between the first battery cell and the second battery cell.

14. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 13, wherein the adhesive layer extends around at least a portion of the first sensor in the plane.

15. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein a portion of the first sensor extends through a gap in the adhesive layer towards an edge of the first battery cell.

16. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned between the first sensor and one of the first battery cell and the second battery cell.

17. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising: a second battery cell stacked on top of the first battery cell, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the second battery cell; a third battery cell stacked on top of the second battery cell; and a second sensor positioned between the third battery cell and the second battery cell for detecting at least one force influencing the third battery cell, wherein each sensor is independently configured to detect forces specific to its respective battery cell without cross-interference.

18. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 17 further comprising a processor configured to: receive a first sensor output signal from the first sensor; receive a second sensor output signal from the second sensor; conduct an evaluation based at least on the received output signals and at least one of voltage, current, and temperature data from the battery cells; and generate at least one processor output signal based on the evaluation.

19. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 18, wherein the processor is further configured to alter an operation of the third battery cell independently from an operation of the first battery cell based on the at least one processor output signal, wherein the alteration is responsive to force conditions detected by the respective sensors.

20. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 18, wherein the processor is further configured to turn off the third battery cell and to maintain operation of the first battery cell based on the at least one processor output signal, wherein the decision to turn off is based on force detection indicating unsafe conditions in the third battery cell.

21. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein the first sensor comprises: force sensing material having a conductance that is configured to vary based on the at least one force influencing the first battery cell; and force sensing circuitry coupled to the force sensing material, wherein the force sensing circuitry is configured to produce a force output signal based on the conductance of the force sensing material, and wherein the force sensing material exhibits a measurable change in electrical properties in response to mechanical deformation.

22. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 21, wherein the force sensing material comprises at least one variable electrical conductor configured to respond to mechanical stress by altering its electrical conductance in a predictable manner.

23. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 22, wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor has a first level of electrical conductance when the at least one variable electrical conductor is quiescent, and wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor has a second level of conductance when a mechanical stress is applied to the at least one variable electrical conductor, wherein the transition between conductance levels is repeatable and reversible.

24. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 22, wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor is a quantum tunneling composite material that exhibits stress-sensitive conductance characteristics suitable for detecting battery cell deformation.

25. (Cancelled)

26. (Cancelled)

27. (Cancelled)

28. (Original) A method for monitoring a battery comprising a first cell and a second cell stacked within an enclosure, the method comprising: positioning a first sensor material between the first cell and one of the second cell and the enclosure; varying the conductance of the first material based on at least one force influencing the first cell; and producing a first force output signal based on the conductance of the first material.

29. (Original) The method of claim 28 further comprising controlling a facility of the first cell based on the force output signal.

30. (Original) The method of claim 28 further comprising: receiving a battery status signal, wherein the battery status signal is responsive to at least one of a voltage, a current, and a temperature of the first cell; evaluating the first force output signal and the battery status signal; and generating at least one evaluated output signal based on the evaluation of the first force output signal and the battery status signal.
